feed.title: NPR Topics: Health
feed.subtitle: Comprehensive health news from NPR. Follow for updates on medical research, wellness trends, public health policy, patient care and healthcare systems.

entry.title: Who makes Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans — and under what conditions?
entry.summary: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?

entry.title: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back
entry.summary: Coal miners who are exposed to silica dust are at a higher risk of black lung disease. Despite decades of advocacy, new efforts to regulate the toxic dust are under threat.

entry.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
entry.summary: The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.

entry.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
entry.summary: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.

entry.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
entry.summary: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.

entry.title: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
entry.summary: He's the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee that oversees health aid and he's just announced he's running for Majority Leader. He spoke to NPR about his foreign aid vision.

entry.title: Happy World Kindness Day! Check out our kind photos of kindness to humans -- and cats
entry.summary: Friday, November 13 is World Kindness Day. Your mission: Do something kind. Small acts of kindness definitely count!

entry.title: Kratom and 7-OH can feel like 'a miracle.' They can also be addictive
entry.summary: In the last decade, strong support for kratom and 7-OH products have kept them federally legal. That's started to change. A crackdown for some highly potent products related to kratom is coming.

entry.title: Fed up with the healthcare industry, this red state capped insulin prices for patients
entry.summary: Republicans and Democrats in North Dakota worked together to limit what people with diabetes have to pay for insulin, joining a growing bipartisan push across the country to protect patients.

entry.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
entry.summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.
